overview: After 2.Nf3 Black plays 2...b5 and usually follows with ...Bb7. White can play 3.g3 and Bg2 or 3.e4 and Bd3 to challenge the odd structure. It is a rare provocation, and the b5 pawn is not easy to attack at once.

white_ideas.idea: Fianchetto with g3 and Bg2 against the ...Bb7
e4 and Bd3 to take the centre
Exploit the weakened c6 and a6 squares

typical_structures.structure: Black queenside pawns advanced early, White centre pawns free

character.notes: Unusual but quiet; neither side forces matters.

gambit.notes: No material is given up on purpose.

soundness.notes: Strong players think White gets a comfortable edge, so dubious for Black.

approach.notes: Played by almost no strong players.

level.notes: Few forced lines; a provocative line is not a first repertoire.

character.reason: Neither forcing nor especially solid; White simply develops against an odd set-up.

gambit.reason: The b5 pawn is not attacked at once and no pawn is offered.

soundness.reason: Black spends time on ...b5 and White gets a comfortable edge.

structure.reason: Neither side has committed the centre.

approach.reason: Almost never chosen by strong players.

level.reason: Simple ideas, but a dubious line is not for beginners.

plans.reason: Black fianchettoes on b7 behind advanced queenside pawns.
